'''Havenstein:''' {{legend0|#FFB2B2|40–50%}} {{legend0|#E27F7F|50–60%}} {{legend0|#D75D5D|60–70%}} {{legend0|#D72F30|70–80%}} {{legend0|#a80000|>90%}} | title = [[Governor of New Hampshire|Governor]] | before_election = [[Maggie Hassan]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Maggie Hassan]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsNH}} The '''2014 New Hampshire gubernatorial election''' was held on November 4, 2014, to elect the [[governor of New Hampshire]], concurrently with the [[United States Senate election in New Hampshire, 2014|election]] to New Hampshire's [[Classes of United States senators|Class II U.S. Senate seat]], as well as other elections to the [[2014 United States Senate elections|United States Senate]] in other states and elections to the [[2014 United States House of Representatives elections|United States House of Representatives]] and various state and local elections. Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] governor [[Maggie Hassan]] ran for re-election to a second term in office. She defeated the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] nominee, businessman [[Walt Havenstein]]. As of {{Year}}, this is the last time a Democrat was elected Governor of New Hampshire. Hassan would retire in 2016 to run successfully for the [[2016 United States Senate election in New Hampshire|Senate]]. ==Background== Incumbent Democratic governor [[John Lynch (New Hampshire governor)|John Lynch]] decided to retire [[2012 New Hampshire gubernatorial election|in 2012]], rather than seek re-election to a fifth term in office. The Democratic nominee, former [[New Hampshire Senate|State Senate]] Majority Leader [[Maggie Hassan]], defeated the Republican nominee, attorney and [[1996 United States gubernatorial elections|1996]] gubernatorial nominee [[Ovide M. Lamontagne]], 55% to 43%. New Hampshire and [[Vermont]] are the only states in the country whose governors are elected every two years. On only one occasion since 1924 has a first-term governor of New Hampshire been defeated for re-election to a second term: in [[2004 New Hampshire gubernatorial election|2004]], when Lynch beat incumbent Republican governor [[Craig Benson]].{{cite web|url=http://www.wmur.com/news/politics/poll-job-approval-ratings-rise-for-hassan/-/9857748/21267234/-/154vlhj/-/index.html|title=Poll: Job approval ratings rise for Hassan|date=July 31, 2013|access-date=August 2, 2013|work=WMUR}}Schweitzer, Sarah (November 4, 2004). "[http://archive.boston.com/news/politics/governors/articles/2004/11/04/defeated_after_1_term_nh_governor_fades_out/ Defeated after 1 term, N.H. governor fades out]". ''[[The Boston Globe]]''. Retrieved on February 6, 2011. Hassan had high approval ratings. An April 2014 [[WMUR-TV|WMUR]]/[[University of New Hampshire]] poll found that 57% of registered voters approved of the job she was doing, 58% had a favorable opinion of her, and 70% thought the state was going in the right direction.{{cite web|url=http://cola.unh.edu/sites/cola.unh.edu/files/research_publications/gsp2013_fall_govapp102413.pdf|title=APPROVAL OF HASSAN AND LEGISLATURE REMAINS HIGH, MOST THINK NH IS ON RIGHT TRACK|date=October 24, 2013|access-date=February 3, 2014|work=WMUR/UNH|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140221013332/http://cola.unh.edu/sites/cola.unh.edu/files/research_publications/gsp2013_fall_govapp102413.pdf|archive-date=February 21, 2014|url-status=dead}} For these reasons, Hassan was not considered vulnerable going into the election.
